clue.text: I’m at Alabama city and I’m not moving

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
Mobile is a port city in Alabama

explanation.surface: A traveller stuck in an Alabama city declares they are going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the speaker in a city; cryptically 'I'm' sits right at the city's name, and the clue ends by describing the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immobile is stationary, fixed in place and unable to move about.

clue.text: Dolly’s role, performing

blocks.note: an actor's role is a part
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: A comment on the part Dolly plays while she is on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dolly’s' reads as Dolly is: the definition followed by a joining verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolly Parton is the famous American country singer, so her surname answers to her first name.

clue.text: After riot her moving, initially calm, speech

indicators.note: letters that are moving get shifted out of their printed order
initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows
After places the chosen letter behind the rearranged group in the final answer

blocks.note: these seven letters rearranged
its first letter

explanation.surface: A call for calm speeches after a woman's riot has stirred things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speaking, and by extension a speech or pompous language itself.

clue.text: For this study several years, or sixty minutes

blocks.note: first meaning: a university qualification earned over years of study
second meaning: a unit of angle divided into sixty minutes of arc

explanation.surface: Weighing a long course of study against a single hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sixty minutes' looks like an hour of clock time, but angles are also divided into minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A university qualification takes years of study, and an angular unit contains sixty arc minutes.

clue.text: Marsupial’s origin? Australian territory, principally

indicators.note: principally means taking the leading letters of the preceding words

blocks.note: the womb is where life originates
first letters of both words

explanation.surface: Asking where a marsupial comes from and answering with an Australian territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marsupial’s' reads as marsupial is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing Australian animal that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Two rhymes for say ‘ambush’

blocks.note: two words that rhyme with say: way and lay, joined

explanation.surface: A rhyming exercise: find two rhymes for the word say.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'ambush' look like the word to be rhymed, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay someone is to lie in wait and stop or attack them unexpectedly.

clue.text: Walk round hospital to get suture

indicators.note: round says one word wraps itself about another

blocks.note: to tread is to walk
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient strolls about the hospital to have stitches done.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons close wounds with stitching material, so a suture is a length of surgical thread.

clue.text: Daughter putting topping on cake and cutting it up?

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
the sugary coating on top of a cake

explanation.surface: A daughter ices a cake and then slices it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicing food means chopping it into small cubes, a particular kind of cutting.

clue.text: Workers’ appearance for informal vote

blocks.note: a show is an appearance
hands are workers; the possessive is read as 'of'

explanation.surface: Workers turn up in order to hold a quick vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Workers’' turns into the word 'of', so the two pieces swap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising hands to be counted is a quick, unofficial way of taking a ballot at a meeting.

clue.text: What’s in this shoe? I don’t believe it!

blocks.note: first meaning: literally the body part belonging to me inside my footwear
second meaning: an exclamation of scornful disbelief

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is taken literally, the second is the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial retort rejecting a claim, and literally names a part of the speaker's body in a shoe.

clue.text: Rare event in field that may involve a couple of ducks

definitions.text: Rare event in field that may involve a couple of ducks

blocks.note: surface reading: something unusual happening out in the countryside
setter's reading: in cricket a duck is a score of nought, so two batters out for nothing in successive balls

explanation.surface: A rare sighting in a meadow involving a pair of waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler taking wickets with three consecutive balls achieves a hat-trick, and new batters dismissed first ball score a duck (nought).
explanation.definitionFit: Three wickets from three successive deliveries is a rare feat, and the dismissed batters may well score nothing.

clue.text: The country of Somalia?

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, a part found inside the following word

blocks.note: the middle four letters

explanation.surface: Asking which nation Somalia is.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a geography question about Somalia; the question mark warns the country is literally inside the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: The port of Salerno?

blocks.note: the question mark asks for a fresh, made-over version of the town's name, and the answer announces it is one
the Italian town's name, whose letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about the harbour of the Italian city Salerno.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is in the answer itself: ORLEANS is a new arrangement of SALERNO, so the port is 'new Orleans'. The question mark flags this trick.
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans is a major Mississippi river port in Louisiana in the United States.

clue.text: Fierce cat: it chewed an official document

indicators.note: something chewed is mangled out of its original shape

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A savage cat has chewed up an important document.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate is a formal paper attesting to a fact, such as a birth or qualification.

clue.text: Film, plays, and a party

blocks.note: to toy with something is to play with it
the Tories are Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A list of entertainments: a film, some plays and a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Toy Story is the 1995 Pixar animated feature about living toys.

clue.text: Sickness noted away from centre in Egyptian city once

indicators.note: away from centre means discarding the middle and keeping only the ends
in places one group of letters inside another

blocks.note: Thebes was a capital of ancient Egypt
its outer letters only

explanation.surface: An illness recorded somewhere outside the centre of an ancient Egyptian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Decompression sickness suffered by divers who surface too quickly is known colloquially by this name.

clue.text: Mendelssohn’s caveman?

blocks.note: surface reading: a prehistoric cave dweller somehow linked to the composer
setter's reading: the legendary hero after whom the Hebridean cave in Mendelssohn's Hebrides overture is named

explanation.walkthrough: Mendelssohn's Hebrides overture is also called Fingal's Cave, after a sea cave on Staffa named for the Celtic hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The cave celebrated in the overture belongs, by name, to the mythical giant Fingal.

clue.text: Better years for glad rags

blocks.note: finer means better
Y is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: Better times ahead call for dressing up in smart clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is informal for one's best clothes, and finery is showy elegant dress.

clue.text: Deny island is to be converted into theme park

indicators.note: converted means changed into a different form

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An official denies that an island will be turned into an amusement resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Disneyland is the famous Californian amusement park built around Disney characters.

clue.text: Time to drop into unpretentious local

indicators.note: to drop into means to fall inside something else

blocks.note: naive means artless and unsophisticated
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It's time to pop into a down-to-earth neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' suggests a British pub, but here it is a noun for a resident of a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is someone born in a place, which is what calling someone a local means.

clue.text: Rule at Christmas? Stop scratching!

indicators.note: at says one word stands next to another, here with it following on

blocks.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A seasonal regulation ordering someone to quit scratching.
explanation.walkthrough: The month abbreviation comes first, so read 'Rule at Christmas' as the rule positioned after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Declawing a cat removes its claws, which stops it from clawing furniture or people.

clue.text: A sign to leave the auditorium

blocks.note: first meaning: the lit notice marking a way out of a building
second meaning: to go out, as an actor does in a stage direction

explanation.surface: A notice telling the audience to go out of the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the notice above a doorway and the verb for departing a stage or room.

clue.text: A fool and an unruly youth become troubled

blocks.note: taken as written
a git is a British slang word for a fool
the indefinite article
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British rebellious youth

explanation.surface: A fool and a teenage tearaway get themselves into a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated means feeling anxious, disturbed and nervously upset.

clue.text: Intelligent means of applying pressure to Conservative

indicators.note: to here means attached onto, so one part joins the end of another

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lever is a bar used to apply force

explanation.surface: A shrewd way to put the squeeze on a Tory politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and intelligent are synonyms for being quick-witted and bright.

clue.text: Uniform not recorded by railway

blocks.note: a live broadcast is not prerecorded
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Something about a railway's dress code that nobody wrote down.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive clothing worn by servants or staff, a form of uniform.

clue.text: After time children’s author is cheap

indicators.note: After puts the following item behind the one named second

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the Rev W. Awdry wrote the Thomas the Tank Engine books

explanation.surface: Over time, a writer of children's books has come to seem tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry describes showy goods of poor quality, gaudy and cheaply made.
